report.summary: Identified 3 cross-file hypotheses: (1) mutable default cache shared across modules, (2) inconsistent handling of external graph nodes, (3) incomplete verification logic in verify_fix_counts.
risks: Mutable default cache in docrefs.py may cause cross-call contamination when shared with other modules using the same dict.
External nodes trimmed from graph in spectral.py may be re-included elsewhere, leading to inconsistent metrics.
verify_fix_counts is incomplete and may allow prose fixes that would otherwise be rejected by verify_fix.
todos: Confirm whether the mutable cache in docrefs.py is ever passed to other modules or used concurrently.
Check if any other module (e.g., in eval) re-inserts external nodes into the graph after spectral.py trims them.
Complete verify_fix_counts or remove it if it is dead code.

hypotheses.claim: The mutable default argument `cache: dict = {}` in `daedalus/spine/docrefs.py:scan()` is shared across all calls, and if any other module (e.g., `daedalus/eval/mint.py`) passes the same dict or relies on its default, cached data may leak between independent scans, causing stale or incorrect results.
hypotheses.mechanism: Python defaults are evaluated once at function definition. Thus, all calls to scan() that omit the cache argument share the same dict. If mint.py calls scan() without providing its own cache, or if it passes a dict that is later reused, modifications to the cache in one call persist and affect subsequent calls. This could cause mint.py to see stale overrides or miss file changes.
hypotheses.refuted_by: If it can be shown that no module ever calls scan() without an explicit cache argument, or that the cache is never reused across independent scans (e.g., always passed as a fresh empty dict), then this hypothesis is refuted.
evidence: daedalus/eval/mint.py: imports but does not call scan() in this chunk; however, the docstring references harness and tasks that may call scan()

hypotheses.claim: `projection_to_graph` in `daedalus/mapping/spectral.py` trims edges to nodes not in `known` (i.e., external modules), but other modules (e.g., `daedalus/eval/mint.py`) may later reintroduce those external nodes as label sources or targets, causing inconsistency: the graph used for metrics excludes them, but the eval subsystem may include them in scoring.
hypotheses.mechanism: spectral.py's `projection_to_graph` deliberately removes edges to nodes outside the scanned tree (see claim: "reach may record an import of something outside the scanned tree... inventing nodes for them would inflate every denominator"). However, mint.py's docstring claims that scope is determined by `cached_index(repo)["modules"]` (the same index used by spectral.py). If mint.py uses a different scope definition (e.g., includes external nodes), then the graph and the eval labels would disagree. This could cause recall scores to be computed against symbols that are not represented in the graph.
hypotheses.refuted_by: If it can be shown that mint.py's scope check (`cached_index(repo)["modules"]`) is identical to the set of `known` nodes used in spectral.py, and that no external nodes ever appear as label sources, then this hypothesis is refuted.
evidence: daedalus/mapping/spectral.py: projection_to_graph trims edges to external nodes (line 1-3)
daedalus/eval/mint.py: docstring claims scope uses cached_index(repo)["modules"] (lines 21-25)

hypotheses.claim: `verify_fix_counts` in `daedalus/spine/docrefs.py` is an incomplete stub that only calls `check_denominator` but does not perform the full verification logic of `verify_fix`. If any caller uses `verify_fix_counts` expecting it to fully validate a prose fix (as suggested by its docstring: "verify_fix with the before-side reduced to its one load-bearing number"), it will accept fixes that would be rejected by `verify_fix`, leading to false positives in the gate.
hypotheses.mechanism: `verify_fix_counts` is defined with an unused parameter `target` and only calls `check_denominator`, returning early if destroyed. It does not execute the rest of `verify_fix` (which presumably checks other conditions). If mint.py or any other module calls `verify_fix_counts` as part of task confirmation (as hinted by the docstring about `confirm_task`), it may approve a fix that actually violates other constraints, bypassing the full verification.
hypotheses.refuted_by: If `verify_fix_counts` is never called by any module (dead code), or if `verify_fix` itself is also incomplete and the missing logic is not essential, then this hypothesis is refuted. Alternatively, if the full `verify_fix` is shown to only call `check_denominator` as well, then `verify_fix_counts` is complete.
evidence: daedalus/spine/docrefs.py: verify_fix_counts body (lines 677-680) only calls check_denominator and returns
daedalus/eval/mint.py: docstring mentions confirm_task and MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD, implying a verification step
